$comment: OBRA Level 1 dialogue. RULE: no line may name a drawable class. Tags appear in exactly one surface form, marked with **. English for now; the Taglish original is kept in level-1-design/files/dialogue_l1.json. NOTE: the Tagalog was masking class references -- tulay/bridge, hagdan/stairs, susi/key, pinto/door, puno/tree -- so a literal translation would have broken the rule in eight lines. Those are phrased around: 'a crossing', 'the way up', 'it', 'one way in', 'old growth'.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: ...Ugh. My head.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I was in Lola's house. I picked up her brush, and the painting on the wall — it moved. It pulled me in.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Where am I? These terraces... those mountains. It smells like rain.
Apo.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Who said that? Hello?
Here. Just behind you.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: AAH! You — you're see-through! You're a GHOST!
Easy, easy. Mind the edge — it is a long way down to the paddy.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: Stay back! Don't come any closer!
lines.text: Stay back! Don't come any closer!
I will stay right here. See? Not one step.
I would never hurt you, apo. Never.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: W-what are you?
A fair question. A strange one to be asked, after all this time.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: This is a dream. I'm going to wake up.
lines.text: This is a dream. I'm going to wake up now. Any second.
Pinch yourself, if you like. It will only hurt.
It is not a dream. Though she would have liked that you thought so.
I am Lolo. That is what everyone in this valley called me, and you may too.
And you, apo, are standing inside one of your Lola's paintings.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Inside a painting? That's impossible.
Look at the light on the walls. Look at the edges of things. Every stroke of it is hers.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: ...It does look like her work. That green she always mixed.
Ask me what you need to. We have a little time before we walk.
What else would you like to know?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Why are you a ghost?
Because she painted me here. On this very terrace, one summer, with my sleeves rolled up.
When a painter loves a place, a little of it stays in the paint. When she loves a person, a little of them stays too.
I am the little that stayed. Paint and memory. Not quite a ghost — not quite not one.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: How did I get in here?
lines.text: How did I get in here?
You picked up her brush. Her paintings are not pictures, apo. They are worlds — every one a place she loved.
And they open for the people she loved. That is you.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Where is Lola?
Not in this one. But she left pieces of herself in all of them.
Follow the pieces, and perhaps we will both understand.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: How do I get home?
Her paintings have worn through in places. Steps fallen, crossings rotted away.
But her brush still works here. Whatever you paint with it, this world believes.
Mend the way through, and the way leads home.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Okay... show me.
Good. I know these terraces better than anyone — she painted me walking them.
Stay close, apo. I will be your guide.
Apo! You came back.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I couldn't stay away.
Neither could she. She painted this valley more times than I can count.
Shall we walk it a different way this time?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Yes. Show me something new.
Then keep your eyes open. Every fork in this valley has more than one answer.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I liked it the way it was.
lines.text: I liked it the way it was.
So did she. But she never painted the same terrace the same way twice.
Welcome back, apo. Last time you mended everything you touched — just as she would have.
This time, try another road. The valley looks different from a different path.
There you are. Last time you found your way around everything. Clever.
But what would happen if you mended it instead? Or made a road of your own?
Back again. Last time you cut your own path through. Strong hands.
There are gentler ways, apo. She would want you to see those too.
You again! You know these terraces nearly as well as I do now.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: You're always here when I come back.
Where else would I be? This is where she painted me.
Apo — did you ever find what she pressed and hid in this valley?
There is a hollow under the far wall. Bring your own light, and look.
Every time you come back, the colours look a little brighter. I think the painting remembers you.
Welcome back, apo. Her stair is waiting.
Her stair is just ahead. She painted it from right here, every morning one summer.
Ang Hagdan, apo. Her stair. Every step of it has fallen.
Look up. Draw something you can **climb**, and set it against the wall.
Up you go. She would have laughed at that, and then she would have used it.
I could not read it, apo. Not wrong — too like something else. Bigger, slower.
There. Now I see it.
Here.
There was a crossing here. Wood. My grandfather's grandfather made it, and made it again.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Two thousand years, the books say.
The books say.
The land does not.
Four hundred years, apo. This was not left behind. It is an answer.
What you are walking on is not old stone. People made it, rather than give up.
I know only three ways. One: make something that can **span** it.
Two: follow the walls. Something that can **leap**, or something that can **climb**.
Three: there is old growth at the forest's edge. Something that can **cut**.
It is up to you. What do we do?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Let us put it back.
She was the same. She never went around a thing — she mended it.
She painted this crossing six times in a day. The water is different every hour.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: There is another way. We go around.
You know, that is how we used to walk. The wall — that is a road, not only an edge.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will make a way.
We crossed.
Someone owns that forest. Not a person. A family.
That was not only wood. That is the water for every terrace below.
There is a hollow under the far wall. She pressed flowers, apo. And she hid them.
You cannot see into it. Not without bringing your own light.
There. One of hers, still where she left it.
She stopped here. Look — her stool, her jar of brushes.
It is in the straw. She hid things there when the rain kept her from the house.
Two ways at a haystack. Get under it — you would have to be small — or take it apart.
We can do it slowly — something that can **forage**, that sifts through.
We can go in underneath — something that can **carry**, that can drag it out.
Or scatter it. Something that can bring **weather**. What is hidden comes out with it.
How patient are you today, apo?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Slowly. Let us look properly.
A brush. Dried out.
Paper. It has a date. And she wrote something in the margin.
'It is still on the nail.' Remember that.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will do it.
Fast. You did not see the rest of it.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: There. The wind scattered it.
You got it.
Ay — you can stand up in here. She kept things in here. Of course she did.
Mind where you step. They were living in here before either of us came looking.
Brass. Too small for that lock. This one belongs somewhere else.
Somewhere she has only ever shown you as a painting. Keep it.
Locked. Of course.
Something that can **cut** would go through that hasp, though.
Her diary. She wrote in it every night, even when the words got harder to find.
There is the house.
No windows. One way in, above head height. And the way up is gone.
You take the way up inside at night. That is the lock. There is nothing else.
But that chest — she carried it up from the lowlands. That one was made to be opened.
We can go up. Something that can **climb** — not the posts, they carry rat guards.
Or something that can **unlock** it. If you can make the right one.
Or something that can **cut**, and the conversation is over.
Which?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: It is inside. Let us find it.
The roof. Under the edge — there is a gap there.
On the nail. Just as she said.
A photograph.
She is young there. That painting is not finished yet.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Lolo — who is that beside her?
Let us go back down.
Do not. Those are not decoration, and they are not yours.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will make something that opens it.
lines.text: I will make something that opens it.
It turned, then stopped. Something in the shape is wrong — it will say which.
Closer. It has named the one thing it measured. Draw to that.
There.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Let us open it.
You opened it.
That is the one. Pista — the plaza, the bunting, the whole town out in the street.
She never hung this one. Carry it carefully, apo.
There is the marker stone. That is where we stopped on the way home.
Someone cut that. Someone meant to lay it on a roof before the rain.
Look at the terrace below. It is drying out.
Pista. She said the noise helped her think.
Apo — look at the edge. The shawl. I know that shawl.
Last time you put the crossing back. The other two ways are still waiting for you.
Last time we went around by the walls. Will you try something else today?
Last time you cut through the old growth. Perhaps a gentler way, this time?
You have tried every way across. Choose whichever your heart likes best.
Last time you sifted it slowly. You could be quicker about it today.
Last time you went in and dragged it out. There are other ways into straw.
Last time the wind took it all. Go gently this time, and see what you missed.
Every way into the straw, you have tried. Pick the one you liked.
Last time you went in under the roof. There are other ways into her house.
Last time you made something to open it. Try another way today?
Last time you cut your way in. She would not have minded — but there are softer ways.
You have opened her house every way there is. Choose the one that felt right.
Welcome back, apo! Still dizzy from all that dancing in the plaza?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: My feet still hurt.
Then walk slowly. The terraces have never once been in a hurry.
Welcome back, apo! Tired of swimming already?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I still have sand in my shoes.
Shake it out on the terraces. The farmers will not mind.
Did you know, apo? The Ifugao carved every one of these terraces into the mountain by hand.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: By hand? All of them?
All of them. Stone, mud and patience. They say if you laid the walls end to end, they would stretch halfway around the world.
These are the Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras, apo. The whole world agreed they are worth keeping — they are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Every terrace drinks from the forest above it. Ifugao families keep their own woodlots — muyong — so the water never stops running down.
Cut the forest, and the terraces go thirsty. That is why it matters what we do up here.
At harvest the Ifugao sing the hudhud — long chanted stories, passed from voice to voice.
Some take days to sing all the way through. UNESCO counts them among the world's treasures too.
Those carved figures by the granaries are bulul, apo. Guardians of the rice — farmers trusted them to keep the harvest plentiful.
Up here they grow an heirloom rice called tinawon. It is planted only once a year, and it takes its time — like everything worth eating.
All over the Philippines, farmers work the paddies with the carabao. Strong, patient, and happiest up to its knees in mud.
We say a meal without rice is not a real meal. Every grain out there was planted by somebody's hands, apo. Remember that at dinner.

conversations.$comment: Scripted exchanges, played by LevelBase._run_conversation. Steps point at hooks and line ids above; nothing here is said that is not a line.

$comment_returns: returns: the replay pool, in two halves by `pool` -- a `greeting` (the route taken last time, the level just come from, how often they have been back) and a `fact` about the real place. One of each plays per return. Within a pool the entry heard fewest times wins (PlayerProfile.dialogue_heard), then highest `priority`, then file order -- so the most relevant comes first and nothing repeats until every eligible one has played.
